questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: For me it was important that the host university offered courses that were relevant for my study and were interesting. Furthermore, I chose Norway as my study destination because of its beautiful nature. In addition, I wanted to study in Europe and a place where I could feel safe during a time with the pandemic.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: For me it has been the best decision in my life to go on an exchange. I have learned so much, both academically, but also about other cultures and about myself.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy. I got all the information I needed via email.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had to pick up my keys at a service center located very close to my student accommodation. The personnel at the service center was very informative and willing to help.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was very easy. 
I was recommended by a friend to stay at Fantoft student housing and I will definitely recommend it as well. It is really modern and has all the facilities you need (gym, common area, rooftop, garden etc.). Many exchange students live at Fantoft, and you really get to know a lot of nice people there.  I lived in a flat with 15 other people from all over Europe (Spain, Italy, Greece, Netherlands, Germany and Denmark) and shared my room with a Dutch girl.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You get to know a lot of other exchange students, which is really nice. I didn't get the opportunity to talk with so many locales, which maybe was a bit unfortunate.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process was a bit of a hassle, because it wasn't entirely clear what courses I was able to take or not. It was first clear after I moved to my study destination in the beginning of the semester, which was too late in my opinion. I think this was due to lack of communication between UCPH and the host university, and I hope for future students that this will be improved.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Email and information on the University's website.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I were very lucky and were able to register for all the classes I wanted to take.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Start in good time to find out which courses you think might be interesting and be sure that you have the right prerequisites for taking the courses. Don't be afraid to contact the host institution and ask questions about any doubts you might have.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took mainly master courses even though I'm a bachelor student, and I actually find the level quit easy. I think it was way easier to get good grades compared to at UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
I think there was more focus on memorization compared to problem solving at UCPH. 
The exams question were mainly multiply choices, which are very different from my exams at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Immunology 
Animal science 
Lipid Biochemistry from chemistry to disease
Developmental genetics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Immunology is a very intense, but interessting course, which gives an introduction to the immune system and its general functions and perspectives to autoimmune diseases and cancer. 

I was really happy about the course lipid biochemistry, because it gives you a deeper understanding of the functions and structures of different lipids, and how these lipids play an important role in many disease like Alzheimers. In this course I also wrote a paper about a specific lipid, which was really interesting.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I went on many trips, which costed a lot of money, but definitely were worth it.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
I already knew that groceries are very expensive in Norway, but vegetables are insanely expensive. In addition, the prices for alcohol are very high (three times Danish prices). 
The prices for fish, especially salmon are fairly cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is an organization called Sammen, which really takes care of students and which offers cheap training facilities, cafeterias and various social activities and events and much more. Especially in the beginning they organize a lot of events to let people meet each other and make friends.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
All outdoor activities. Hiking in Norway is absolutely amazing and is the perfect break for studying. 
I also climbed a lot, which was so much fun.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Explore the old part of the city and the harbor, it is very cozy. 
Experience the beautiful nature is a must.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. Norwegians are very similar to Danes, and are very friendly.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
I socialized mostly with other international exchange students, but if you want to socialize more with locals you can for example become a volunteer in different student organisations or debate clubs. 
In one of the first week of the semester, we had a tutor-week arranged by the University, where we met up with older Norwegian students from our Faculty and did a lot of games together. We had a lot of fun.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The Norwegians relation to the nature and healthy mentality.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be openminded and curious, pack some good hiking shoes, and be aware that you are gonna spend a lot of money (it is worth it).

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: My friendships with people from all over Europe and the amazing memories we have together.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
To speak English in the beginning, but you get use to it fast. 
The mountain Lyderhorn :-)

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
